meta.scope: Yemen Batch 4 — Fiscal balance, education disruption, and health/nutrition densification under severe conflict constraints.

candidates.title: Fiscal balance and revenue statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from IMF-aligned and national fiscal monitoring
candidates.description: Fiscal revenue, expenditure and balance indicators. Government revenues (excluding grants) have collapsed relative to pre-war levels; deficits are financed under extreme constraint with heavy reliance on grants and limited domestic sources. Dual control further fragments fiscal capacity.
candidates.notes: Core fiscal-flow node under extreme revenue collapse and dual institutions.

candidates.title: Education disruption and out-of-school statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from UNICEF and education monitoring sources
candidates.description: Statistics and framing of education access under conflict. Millions of children remain out of school; thousands of schools are damaged or destroyed. Continuously cited in humanitarian and human-capital analysis.
candidates.notes: Core education densification under conflict disruption.

candidates.title: Health access and nutrition statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from UNICEF / WHO and humanitarian sources
candidates.description: Statistics on health-service access and malnutrition. Large shares of the population lack access to basic healthcare; severe acute malnutrition among children remains a critical emergency indicator.
candidates.notes: Core health and nutrition densification under humanitarian emergency conditions.

candidates.title: Yemen fiscal–education–health densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from fiscal, education and health sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding fiscal balance/revenue statistics, education disruption, and health/nutrition statistics into a coherent fiscal and human-capital residual layer under severe conflict constraints.
